ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a spiral filling of numbers on grid paper, with 1 written in the gray-marked center square; the adjacent square to the right from this square is 2, then the spiral path goes downward to 3, then left through 4, 5, and afterward continues upward. It can be seen that the spiral direction pattern is right, down, left, up, and the side lengths in order are 1,1,2,2,3,3,.... Then reason: Set the gray-marked square as coordinate (0,0), with upward as the positive y direction, and what is required is (0,100). For the r-th layer spiral, the upper-right corner (r,r) is the completion point of the square of this layer whose side length is 2r+1, so its corresponding position number is (2r+1)^2; the first few layers in the figure also conform, for example (1,1) is the 9th position, and (2,2) is the 25th position. The square directly above, (0,r), is on the top side, r squares left from the upper-right corner (r,r), therefore its position number is (2r+1)^2 - r. Substituting r=100 gives n=(201)^2-100=40401-100=40301. The filled-in numbers repeat periodically as 1,2,3,4,5, and the number at position n is determined by n mod 5. 40301 divided by 5 leaves remainder 1, so the number in that square is 1.

method.method_draft: Use a square-spiral layer formula. From the image, read that the marked gray center cell contains the first digit 1, then the spiral proceeds right to 2, down to 3, left through 4,5, then up, so the direction pattern is right, down, left, up with side lengths 1,1,2,2,3,3,... Let the marked cell be coordinate (0,0), and the requested cell be (0,100). For ring r, the top-right corner (r,r) is reached at sequence position (2r+1)^2, as verified by the visible first rings: (1,1) has position 9 and (2,2) has position 25. The cell (0,r) lies r steps left of (r,r) along the top side, so its sequence position is (2r+1)^2-r. Substitute r=100 to get position 40301. Since the written digits repeat 1,2,3,4,5, the digit at position n is determined by n mod 5; 40301 ≡ 1 mod 5, so the digit is 1.

method.method_draft: Use a layer-to-layer recurrence for the cells directly above the center. From the image, identify the target line as the vertical column through the marked cell, and observe initial positions on that column: center is position 1, one cell above is reached at position 8, two cells above at position 23. In this spiral orientation, to go from the cell (0,r-1) to the next one above it, (0,r), the path must finish the current top side/right side/bottom/left side portions of the next ring; equivalently the sequence-position increase is 8r-1. Thus define a_r as the sequence position at the cell r cells above the marked cell, with a_0=1 and a_r=a_{r-1}+8r-1. Then a_100=1+sum_{r=1}^{100}(8r-1)=1+8(100·101/2)-100=40301. Reduce this position modulo the period 5 of the digit string 12345; 40301 leaves remainder 1, so the cell contains digit 1.
